chunks: And ʿAlī, peace be upon him, said:

A salat (prayer) in Bayt al-Maqdis is equal to one thousand prayers, and a salat (prayer) in al-Masjid al-Aʿẓam is equal to one hundred thousand prayers, and a salat (prayer) in the mosque of the tribe is equal to twenty-five prayers, and a salat (prayer) in the market mosque is equal to twelve prayers, and a man’s salat (prayer) in his house is equal to one prayer.

key_terms.اَلْمَسْجِدِ اَلْأَعْظَمِ: the Greatest Mosque, referring to the most exalted mosque in reward
key_terms.بَيْتِ اَلْمَقْدِسِ: Bayt al-Maqdis, Jerusalem, a sacred place of prayer
key_terms.بَيْتِهِ: his house, the home in which one may perform salat (prayer)
key_terms.تَعْدِلُ: is equal to, denotes equivalence in reward
key_terms.صَلَاةٌ: salat (prayer), the act of ritual worship being compared in reward
key_terms.مَسْجِدِ اَلسُّوقِ: the market mosque, a mosque located in the marketplace
key_terms.مَسْجِدِ اَلْقَبِيلَةِ: the mosque of the tribe, a local communal mosque

ai.seo_question: What is the reward of praying in Bayt al-Maqdis, the Great Mosque, the tribal mosque, and the market mosque?
ai.summary: This hadith states the differing degrees of reward for performing salat (prayer) in various places. It highlights the special merit of sacred and communal mosques while also noting the ordinary reward of praying at home.
